newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet says moving toward profitability.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet says moving toward profitability.

text.p: ValuJet Inc said Thursday it continues "to make fundamental progress" in its efforts to return to profitability following the May 1996 crash that killed 110 people and forced the discount flier to suspend operations for four months.

ValuJet has been operating at a loss since its return to the air on a limited basis in September 1996. But airline president and chief executive officer D. Joseph Carr said it now has a strong balance sheet and strengthened position.

"ValuJet continues to make fundamental progress in its plan to return the airline to consistent levels of profitability," Carr said in a written statement accompanying ValuJet's 1997 second quarter results.

"ValuJet's solid operational results, strong balance sheet, including almost $150 million cash, and announced merger with AirWays Corp are evidence of ValuJet's commitment to strengthening its position in the industry."
ValuJet and AirWays announced their merger plans earlier this month. ValuJet would buy AirWays in a stock deal valued at $61.8 million.

The deal is subject to shareholder, bondholder and regulatory approvals. Following its completion, ValuJet would cease operating under the name that has become linked with the crash of Atlanta-bound Flight 592 in the Florida Everglades.

ValuJet's second quarter loss narrowed slightly from a year ago. It recorded a net loss of $9.2 million, or $0.17 per share, on revenues of $47.8 million versus a loss a year ago of $9.6 million, or $0.18 per share, on revenues of $77.9 million.
During the second quarter 1997, ValuJet resumed service to Dallas/Fort Worth and initiated non-stop service between Atlanta and Flint, Mich., it said.

ValuJet also established its "FlightLink" shuttle service from Atlanta's Hartsfield International Airport to Macon and Dalton, Ga., and to Chattanooga, Tenn. Also, ValuJet joined the Sabre and Worldspan computer reservation systems with display capabilities. On-line booking capabilities will be available in the near future.
